status: image-collated draft, not an independent palaeographic certification
source: Vatican Library Vat.gr.1209, printed manuscript pages 64-65, IIIF canvases p0068-p0069
hand_policy: Visible main-text letter sequence; accents, breathings and retracing not assigned to first hand. No B* claim. Overbars represented in expansion records; word divisions are editorial.
count_policy: Greek alphabet letters only; lunate sigma is represented as capital sigma, a one-to-one recoding. Spaces, punctuation, accents, diaeresis and abbreviation marks are excluded. Contracted names and line-end nasal suspensions have separate layers. Verse boundaries are modern analytical labels.

19.expanded: ΕΞΗΡΕΝ ΔΕ Ο ΑΓΓΕΛΟΣ ΤΟΥ ΘΕΟΥ Ο ΠΡΟΠΟΡΕΥΟΜΕΝΟΣ ΤΗΣ ΠΑΡΕΜΒΟΛΗΣ ΤΩΝ ΥΙΩΝ ΙΣΡΑΗΛ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΟΡΕΥΘΗ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΟΠΙΣΘΕΝ ΕΞΗΡΕΝ ΔΕ ΚΑΙ Ο ΣΤΥΛΟΣ ΤΗΣ ΝΕΦΕΛΗΣ ΑΠΟ ΠΡΟΣΩΠΟΥ ΑΥΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΣΤΗ ΕΚ ΤΩΝ ΟΠΙΣΩ ΑΥΤΩΝ
19.translation: The angel of God who went before the camp of the sons of Israel moved and went behind them; the pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.

20.expanded: ΚΑΙ ΕΙΣΗΛΘΕΝ ΑΝΑ ΜΕΣΟΝ ΤΩΝ ΑΙΓΥΠΤΙΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΑΝΑ ΜΕΣΟΝ ΤΗΣ ΠΑΡΕΜΒΟΛΗΣ ΙΣΡΑΗΛ ΚΑΙ ΕΣΤΗ ΚΑΙ ΕΓΕΝΕΤΟ ΣΚΟΤΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΝΟΦΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΔΙΗΛΘΕΝ Η ΝΥΞ ΚΑΙ ΟΥ ΣΥΝΕΜΙΞΑΝ ΑΛΛΗΛΟΙΣ ΟΛΗΝ ΤΗΝ ΝΥΚΤΑ
20.translation: It came between the Egyptians and the camp of Israel and stood; darkness and gloom arose, the night passed, and they did not mingle with one another throughout the night.

21.expanded: ΕΞΕΤΕΙΝΕΝ ΔΕ ΜΩΥΣΗΣ ΤΗΝ ΧΕΙΡΑ ΕΠΙ ΤΗΝ ΘΑΛΑΣΣΑΝ ΚΑΙ ΥΠΗΓΑΓΕΝ ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ΤΗΝ ΘΑΛΑΣΣΑΝ ΕΝ ΑΝΕΜΩ ΝΟΤΩ ΒΙΑΙΩ ΟΛΗΝ ΤΗΝ ΝΥΚΤΑ ΚΑΙ ΕΠΟΙΗΣΕΝ ΤΗΝ ΘΑΛΑΣΣΑΝ ΞΗΡΑΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΣΧΙΣΘΗ ΤΟ ΥΔΩΡ
21.translation: Moses stretched his hand over the sea; the Lord drove the sea with a violent south wind all night, made the sea dry, and the water was divided.

corroboration.source: Swete, Old Testament in Greek, volume I, printed p132; scanned leaf157 in Internet Archive GRCSWET_DBS_HS
corroboration.observation: Expanded main-text wording agrees at Exodus14:19-21. The 14:20 apparatus reports that A and F prefix ΤΗΣ ΠΑΡΕΜΒΟΛΗΣ to ΤΩΝ ΑΙΓΥΠΤΙΩΝ; no hand attribution is inferred from absence of a note.
